pages.text: Burning fuel in the reactor produces $(bold)Exhausted Fuel$() - hazardous waste that must travel the waste-pipe system. The Life Activator is the $(bold)first neutralization step$(): it slowly activates exhausted fuel into the matching $(bold)activated fluid$().$(br)Activated fluid is no longer waste and can be safely moved by normal fluid pipes.

$(bold)How it works:$()$(li)Input: waste pipes (only exhausted fuel accepted, 7 types can mix)$(li)Convert: $(bold)100 Life Energy$() per mB, at $(bold)4 mB/tick$()$(li)Output: normal fluid pipes (7 activated fluids match their source fuels)$(br2)$(bold)Note:$() activation makes waste safe but does not remove it - activated fluid still needs a consumer (see "Life Centrifuge").
